reasons.reader_question: The queen hands the first-name choice to them, and Devan's glance from his dead pen hand to the lamp points at Neela. Specific and loaded.
reasons.change: Devan learns Asha died comforted, Vellan is dead, and the crown hands the Company its charter question. Knowledge, relationship and power all move.
reasons.romance_movement: There is a new reason here: one shared grief that neither has to forgive. 'Neither would put down and neither would carry alone' lands it.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Her hand checking his shoulder 'as though checking a latch', the held wrist and the two-armed hold all work. The care is shown through action, not narrated.
reasons.character_logic: Vellan, Neela and the queen behave plausibly. Devan standing and walking down hours after a spear through the lung strains belief, and nobody objects.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The queen states the roll's price exactly: bound to the vote, first name the crown answers to. The next decision clearly costs.
reasons.prose: Mostly clean and concrete. There is overtelling ('He was dead. There would be no coming back'), a muddled forgiveness line and an echoed 'lighter than expected' beat.
reasons.continuity: Geography conflicts with F902. The narrow place is at the top of the cut, below Kettamala, yet they carry Vellan 'down' to the lower court. Vellan (~40) is called 'old man'.

fixes: Continuity, at 'They carried him down on the door. Devan walked.' and 'The cut ran down in the new light': the narrow place is at the top of the cut, below Kettamala (F902, F931). Make the procession climb on to the lower court, e.g. 'They carried him up the last of the cut'. Also replace both 'the old man' with 'the big man'. Vellan is about forty (bible: 39).

Overtelling, at 'He was dead. There would be no coming back from it.': the beat's 'stays dead' has leaked onto the page as narration. Cut both sentences and end the scene on the bird line. Also, at 'I'm not forgiving you,' the line reads as refusal. Make it 'Don't ask me to forgive you. There's nothing there to forgive.' Devan's literal voice then stays clear.

Echo dilution, at 'I thought it would be a harder thing to see them go': this repeats Vellan's 'heavier to put down. It isn't' in the same chapter, and so does 'It is very light.' Give the queen her own register of cruel facts. For example, she names the four unready guards' pages as the four she can still be made to read. Keep 'light' for Vellan and the lamp.
reader_question: Who will write the first name on the Company's roll, knowing it makes her the crown's first name to answer?
new_facts_assessment: The roll-price fact (F959) is necessary, consistent with the bible's book 3 ending and well placed. The stair fact (F960) moves the bear from the landing (beat, F954) to the eleventh-step grate. That is logically better, since the postern is where he entered (F592) and Asha descending would meet the landing first. It contradicts F954, so F954 must be retired explicitly.
